done_when: At close, an item that may not change settings and carries a forge.toml different from main's gets main's copy back (its version pin line kept), committed with one printed line; the worker's settings restore takes main's side of an open merge; tests cover a Codex round that merged main's changed settings, on new and adopted repos

known.title: Exclude initial migrations from restoring default settings
Allow the worker to finish a merge containing incoming settings

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 4 (floor: migration)
Raise: Functional — Closing a normal migration now deletes its newly created forge.toml and fails. src/forge/migrate.py:170 defines a Done-when without the literal `forge.toml`, so settings_allowed returns false; the migration creates that file at lines 634–642 while origin/main still has no copy. This restore removes the file from the index and worktree, and the following read raises FileNotFoundError. Preserve migration-owned settings until their initial pull request merges.
findings.title: Exclude initial migrations from restoring default settings

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional — Restoring incoming settings leaves the normal commit nudge unable to finish the merge. worker.py:330–337 asks the successful Codex worker to commit remaining changes, but githooks.py:129–134 rejects every worker commit with forge.toml staged, including these unchanged incoming settings. Unlike the previous restoration, this leaves that forbidden staged difference intact, so the nudge encounters the same refusal and the merge remains open. The new evidence beyond the recorded initial hook refusal is this blocked post-restoration commit. The new test avoids that path by forcing a failed turn and finishing the merge outside the worker at test_close_preserves_default_settings.py:66–76.
findings.title: Allow the worker to finish a merge containing incoming settings

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Functional — Close continues using stale settings after committing main's restored configuration. `cfg` was loaded at close.py:98 and is still passed to review.run at line 336 and checks.wait at line 451. For example, when main removes or renames a required check, this repair writes the current check list but close still waits for the obsolete check and refuses despite all current checks passing. Reload the repaired configuration before subsequent review and check decisions.
findings.title: Reload configuration after repairing forge.toml

why: After a Codex round merges main, the branch can still carry its older forge.toml, so the squash merge reverts main's settings (issue 921, Codex path)
